data.text: PMID 42170804: "Development of polyphenotypic scores to prioritize detection of G6PD rs1050828 heterozygotes in African and African American populations." (Genet Med, 2026). Abstract: Development of polyphenotypic scores to prioritize detection of G6PD rs1050828 heterozygotes in African and African American populations.. PURPOSE: The G6PD missense variant rs1050828 (NP_000393.4:p.Val98Met) is common in African and African American populations. It lowers HbA1c levels independent of glycemia, increasing the risk of underdiagnosis or delayed diagnosis of diabetes. We aimed to develop polyphenotypic scores (PPS) using routinely collected phenotypes to identify likely heteroygotes. METHODS: Using data from 31,083 African or African American participants in the All of Us Research Program, we developed sex-specific PPS through multistage variable selection. We validated the PPS in independent African or African American individuals from All of Us Research Program (N = 8846), BioMe Biobank (N = 8839), and UK Biobank (N = 6811) and evaluated their utility among individuals without diagnosed diabetes. Abstract: Hemoglobin A1c Genetics and Disparities in Risk of Diabetic Retinopathy in Individuals of Genetically Inferred African American/African British and European Ancestries.. data.summary: The variant rs1050828 in G6PD is classified as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic by ClinVar. This variant is associated with altered risk of toxicity to certain antimalarial drugs, such as artesunate, primaquine, pyrimethamine, and sulfadoxine, particularly in pediatric patients. Additionally, it is linked to lower HbA1c levels, which may impact the diagnosis and management of diabetes in individuals of African and African American ancestry.

data.title: Grounded Interpretation
data.content:
The variant rs1050828 in G6PD is classified as Pathogenic/Likely pathogenic by ClinVar. This variant is associated with altered risk of toxicity to certain antimalarial drugs, such as artesunate, primaquine, pyrimethamine, and sulfadoxine, particularly in pediatric patients. Additionally, it is linked to lower HbA1c levels, which may impact the diagnosis and management of diabetes in individuals of African and African American ancestry.

**Limitations:**
- Ensembl could not be reached; this report is partial.
- Ensembl variant effect prediction was unavailable due to an issue with Ensembl.
- The evidence for the clinical significance of the variant is primarily based on pharmacogenomic studies and may not fully capture all potential clinical implications.
